economic_rationale.value: Frog-in-the-pan (limited attention): investors are inattentive to information arriving continuously in small amounts and process it with a delay, so momentum is stronger and more persistent after continuous information than after discrete information with similar cumulative formation-period returns.
economic_rationale.quote: Speciﬁcally, the FIP hypothesis predicts that investors process continuous information with a delay.

universe_and_filters.value: CRSP stocks (returns adjusted for delistings), 1927 to 2007 sample; $5 price filter imposed at the beginning of each month. Share-code, exchange, and breakpoint-universe filters not stated; the data section also says negative book values are eliminated from the sample.

value: monthly stock returns (formation-period and holding-period returns)
required_inputs.quote: We obtain return data from the Center for Research in Security Prices

signal_formula_words.value: Information discreteness (ID): the sign of the formation-period cumulative return (PRET) times the percentage of formation-period days with negative daily returns minus the percentage with positive daily returns. Daily return signs are equally weighted, ignoring magnitude. Small (low) ID = continuous information; large (high) ID = discrete information. Stocks are first sorted on PRET, then on ID.
signal_formula_words.quote: Our benchmark ID proxy is determined by the sign of daily returns and ignores their magnitude by equally weighting each observed return.

signal_formula_symbols.value: ID = sgn(PRET) × [%neg − %pos]; sgn(PRET) = +1 when PRET > 0 and −1 when PRET < 0

formation_window.value: 12 months: PRET is the cumulative return over the past twelve months after skipping the most recent month; ID uses the daily returns of the same formation period
formation_window.quote: PRET is deﬁned as a ﬁrm’s cumulative return over the past twelve months after skipping the most recent month.

skip_window.quote: are reported for each ID quintile after skipping one intermediate month.

holding_period.quote: Post-formation returns over the next six months and three years are then computed.

breakpoints.quote: The results in Panel A pertain to sequential double-sorts involving PRET quintiles, then ID quintiles.

favored_group.value: past winners (highest PRET quintile) in the lowest-ID (continuous information) subportfolio
favored_group.quote: returns from an enhanced momentum strategy that buys past winners and sells past losers following continuous information.

disfavored_group.value: past losers (lowest PRET quintile) in the lowest-ID (continuous information) subportfolio
disfavored_group.quote: Panel A of Table2 reports that momentum, the six-month return from buying winners and selling losers, decreases monotonically from 5.94% in the low ID quintile containing stocks with continuous information to –2.07% in the high ID quintile containing stocks with discrete information.

weighting.quote: Post-formation returns over the next six months and three years are then computed.

expected_sign.quote: Consistent with the FIP hypothesis, continuous information induces stronger and more persistent return continuation than discrete information after conditioning on the magnitude of formation-period returns.

headline_result.value: Six-month momentum (winners minus losers) is 5.94% (t = 4.63) in the continuous-information (low ID) quintile versus –2.07% in the discrete (high ID) quintile; the 8.01% difference has a t-statistic of 8.54 (post-1927).
headline_result.quote: This 8.01% difference in momentum has a t-statistic of 8.54 during the post-1927 sample period.

adaptation.execution: signal through prior month's last close; execute at next month's first trading-day close; new weights earn only after execution

data.universe: 415 names from snapshot; eligible from S&P 500 add date; survivor universe

robustness.holds_definition: alpha t-statistic > 0 and net CAGR above the EW universe

assumptions: 2/20 with a 5% hard hurdle on a long-only equity strategy is an assumption, not an observed fee schedule
no subscriptions or redemptions; AUM is fixed at starting_aum plus returns net of fees
incremental fees are measured versus an equal-weight universe fund charged the same fee schedule, never versus SPY
end_wealth_strategy and end_wealth_ew are net of fees; end_wealth_spy is gross (no fee)
fees are discounted at year-end of each crystallization year; management fees accrue daily and are aggregated per year
break-even AUM scales expected incremental fees linearly with AUM and is reported, not headlined; None when expected incremental fees are not positive
the bootstrap resamples historical days jointly (stationary, geometric blocks); it cannot create regimes absent from the sample
the demeaned run subtracts the historical mean daily excess return over the EW fund from the strategy, testing NPV with no alpha beyond noise structure
synthetic 252-day trading calendar; hurdle accrues on calendar days/365

rubric.rules:
Flags (each computed from results.json):
1. implementation_reliability: green if n_assumed <= 3 AND evidence_valid_rate >= 0.8 AND no critical check-pass disagreements (check-pass items on signal_formula_words, signal_formula_symbols, formation_window, skip_window, holding_period, sort_rule, favored_group, expected_sign); amber if not green and n_assumed <= 6; red otherwise.
2. historical_performance: positive if strategy net CAGR > EW universe CAGR AND strategy net Sharpe > EW universe Sharpe; mixed if exactly one holds; negative if neither; unknown if either input is missing.
3. robustness: a test 'holds' when the alpha t-statistic is > 0 (sign only; the t-statistic is reported, not a gate) AND net CAGR exceeds the EW universe CAGR. strong if it holds at 25 bps AND in both sub-periods AND the ranked-group Spearman rho is in the expected direction; moderate if it holds at 10 bps AND in at least one sub-period; weak otherwise (missing inputs count as not holding).
4. economics: from the fraction of Monte Carlo paths with incremental-fee NPV (vs the EW universe fund, less research cost) > 0: positive if >= 0.6; uncertain if >= 0.4 and < 0.6; negative if < 0.4; unknown if missing.
5. limitations: count = n_assumed + n_adapted (reported, not a gate).
Recommendation (first match wins):
a. 'unable to evaluate' if results status is blocked or incomplete.
b. 'pursue' if performance positive AND robustness strong AND economics positive AND reliability green.
c. 'deprioritize' if performance negative OR (robustness weak AND economics negative).
d. 'investigate further' otherwise.

recommendation_reasons: Historical performance is negative: net CAGR 11.87% vs 12.71% for the EW universe; Sharpe 0.58 vs 0.65.
Robustness is weak: the edge over the EW universe fails at 10 bps, holds in 0 of 2 sub-periods, group rho 1.00 in the expected direction; alpha t -0.99 (reported, not a gate).
Economics are uncertain: P(NPV > 0) 43%, median incremental fee PV -$496k vs the EW universe fund.
Implementation reliability is amber: 4 fields assumed, 6 adapted, evidence valid for 100% of material fields, 0 critical check disagreements.
